page: Microsoft Azure E48d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography. The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

This server includes 1843 GB of local SSD storage, providing fast read and write capabilities directly attached to the instance. In benchmark evaluations, the E48d_v5 demonstrates strong performance, particularly in database operations and memory access, as evidenced by its top-tier Passmark memory and database scores. It also shows strong capabilities in image processing and text generation for small language models, though it exhibits weaker performance on large-scale 70B parameter model text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48d_v5 offers high resource density by bundling substantial memory capacity with a large local SSD, reducing the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput workloads. This hardware profile is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, relational database management systems, large-scale caching layers, data analytics, and enterprise applications requiring a high memory-to-vCPU ratio.
description: Microsoft Azure E48d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at 2.8 GHz, this instance features 1843 GB of local SSD storage and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The processor includes a 48 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and AES cryptography instructions. Benchmark results indicate strong performance in database operations, memory throughput, and image processing, alongside average multi-core CPU performance. In benchmarks, it achieves 44.0 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 39.67 GB per second in static web serving throughput. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core makes this server highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads. It is designed for enterprise databases, large-scale caching, and data analytics pipelines.
